keyVerseText: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
rootMeaning: The word ἐπιφώσκω (epiphṓskō) is derived from the root ἐπιφαύω (epiphaúō), which means 'to give light' or 'to illuminate.' This etymology highlights the concept of light emerging or increasing, specifically the process of growing towards daylight or dawn. Unlike the general English glosses such as 'dawn' or 'draw on,' the root sense emphasizes the active unfolding or shining forth of light, suggesting a dynamic transition from darkness to illumination.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐπιφώσκω appears only twice, with translations including 'as it began to dawn' and 'drew on.' These renderings consistently reflect the idea of light beginning to appear or time progressing toward daylight. The limited but focused usage underscores its role in describing the physical and metaphorical transition from darkness to light, reinforcing its association with beginnings and new phases in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ἐπιφώσκω carries profound significance as it symbolizes the dawning of new hope and the illumination brought by Christ. The imagery of light breaking through darkness aligns with the gospel message of Jesus as the light of the world, overcoming spiritual darkness. Understanding this word in its original sense enriches our appreciation of biblical moments that mark divine intervention or revelation, reminding believers of God's power to bring light and life where there was once darkness.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 28:1, the phrase 'as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week' uses ἐπιφώσκω to set the scene of the resurrection morning. This word conveys the gradual emergence of light, symbolizing the arrival of new life and hope as Mary Magdalene and the other Mary approach the tomb. The dawning light metaphorically points to the resurrection's transformative power, illuminating the darkness of death and signaling the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan.
